What the numbers say

In this revision 137 option-selling candidates across 29 underlyings passed the report's filters, all of them short puts. Expiries run from 2 to 116 days out with a median of 11 days; 50 of the 137 expire within seven days and 8 are more than 21 days out.

The highest composite score is 72.8 for the SOXL 39 put expiring 2026-12-11 (18 days): premium $5.15, strike 10.5% below the share price, model probability of expiring out of the money 51.2%. Its displayed annualized yield of 267.8% multiplies a 18-day premium out to a full year, which is why the score discounts yields from contracts shorter than 30 days.

Implied volatility among the listed contracts is highest for SOXL (209.6%), AMD (133.4%), IREN (129.9%) and lowest for COST (31.0%). High implied volatility is what makes a premium large; it is the market's price for a wide expected range, so the richest premiums sit on the names the market expects to move most.

Of the 37 underlyings with a quote, 34 were up and 3 down when the report was generated; the median move was +6.06%. Rising share prices move existing short puts further out of the money and shrink the premium available on new ones.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-20), listed candidates went from 119 to 137 and the median time to expiry went from 7 to 11 days.

Backtest reference

The report carries a fixed reference backtest covering 2026-03-26 to 2026-04-22: 2,149 simulated option-selling trades with a 83.3% win rate and a profit factor of 0.70. A profit factor below 1 means total losses exceeded total gains even though most trades won. That is the characteristic risk of selling premium: many small wins and a few large losses. The window is short and does not include the session on this page; it is a description of that period, not an estimate of future results.
